baseline.name: Three-reversal array rotation
baseline.approach: Reverse the whole array, then reverse each of the two rotation segments.

archived.name: Repeated one-position right shifts
archived.time: O(n*(k mod n)), where n=numsSize; worst case O(n^2)
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary space; input is modified

why: The archive saves space, but its repeated shifts revisit every element for each residual rotation; it is not the linear three-reversal algorithm.
quantitative_comparison: For n>1 and 1<=r=k mod n<n, the archived source makes n*r array writes. Three reversals perform floor(n/2)+floor(r/2)+floor((n-r)/2) swaps, at most n swaps or 2n array writes. Both can return immediately when r=0. This is a write-count model; it is not a runtime ratio. A small r can favor simple shifts, while r growing with n gives quadratic work.
tradeoffs: Both mutate the array and use constant extra state. The archive is simple but has no overall time-complexity advantage over reversal.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
